title: The Comparative Effectiveness of Vector Control Approaches for Dengue: A Systematic Review and Multilevel Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dengue vector control plays an important role in reducing the burden of dengue infection. Conventional meta‐analysis can only include interventions that can be directly compared. Hence, this study aimed to compare the effectiveness of all interventions for dengue vector control directly and indirectly through a multilevel Bayesian network meta‐analysis. Methods Cluster randomised controlled trials (cRCTs) and randomised controlled trials (RCTs) were included. Screening and full‐text review were performed independently by two reviewers, with resolution by a third reviewer if there was disagreement. Outcomes measured for the included studies considered were entomological indices and epidemiological measures. The Cochrane risk of bias tool was used to assess the quality of the studies by two independent reviewers, with a third reviewer to resolve any discrepancies. Results A total of 48 cRCTs and 13 RCTs were included in this study. The quality of cRCTs and RCTs was overall deemed at high risk of bias except for two studies with low risk of bias. The network meta‐analyses and narrative synthesis indicate that most interventions are not significantly superior to one another. Despite the lack of statistically significant results in the network meta‐analyses, a standalone intervention appears to be less effective than combined interventions. Conclusions Although most interventions were not found to be significantly superior to one another in the network meta‐analyses, it is noteworthy that standalone interventions were shown to be less effective than combined interventions. These results reinforce the importance of promoting integrated, multi‐faceted vector control strategies for dengue prevention.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and multilevel network meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of various vector control interventions for dengue. The study included 48 cluster randomised controlled trials (cRCTs) and 13 randomised controlled trials (RCTs). The findings suggest that most interventions are not significantly superior to one another, but combined interventions appear more effective than standalone ones. The review highlights the need for integrated, multi-faceted vector control strategies to prevent dengue. The results emphasize the importance of using comprehensive approaches in dengue vector control.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 登革热 媒介 控制在减轻登革热感染负担方面发挥着重要作用。传统的荟萃分析只能包括可以直接比较的干预措施。因此,本研究旨在通过多级贝叶斯网络荟萃分析直接和间接比较所有干预措施对登革热 媒介 控制的有效性。方法 包括整群随机对照试验(cRCT)和随机对照试验(RCT)。筛选和全文审阅由两名审稿人独立进行,如果存在分歧,则由第三名审稿人解决。所考虑的纳入研究的测量结果是昆虫学指数和流行病学措施。两名独立评审员使用 Cochrane 偏倚风险工具评估研究质量,并由第三名评审员解决任何差异。结果本研究共纳入48个cRCT和13个RCT。除两项具有低偏倚风险的研究外,cRCT 和 RCT 的质量总体上被认为具有高偏倚风险。网络荟萃分析和叙述综合表明,大多数干预措施并不明显优于其他干预措施。尽管网络荟萃分析缺乏统计上显着的结果,但独立干预措施似乎不如联合干预措施有效。结论 尽管在网络荟萃分析中并未发现大多数干预措施明显优于其他干预措施,但值得注意的是,单独干预措施的效果不如联合干预措施。这些结果强调了促进综合、多方面的 媒介 控制策略对登革热预防的重要性。

title: Deep learning with multiscale spatial context improves global dengue suitability mapping
abstract: Abstract Infectious-disease risk models often rely on occurrence records that are incomplete and spatially biased by surveillance effort, diagnostic access, and outbreak history. Ecological niche modelling (ENM) can identify areas where disease occurrence is environmentally plausible, yet most approaches represent locations using only pointwise covariate values and therefore overlook the surrounding spatial context and rely on presence-only data. Here, we present a deep-learning framework for presence-only data that estimates relative disease suitability by comparing the environmental conditions surrounding reported occurrences with those sampled across the wider study area. The model processes gridded environmental patches at local, neighbourhood, and broader landscape scales, learns the contribution of each scale, and accommodates missing raster values. Using dengue virus as a global case study, we evaluate whether multiscale spatial representation improves upon point-based ENM baselines including random forest and maximum entropy (MaxEnt) under a spatially disjoint train-test design. The model achieved a Boyce index of 0.971 and an AUC of 0.976 on the held-out test set. Learned scale weights and ablation experiments indicated that neighbourhood context contributed most strongly, while local and broader-scale information provided complementary predictive signals. Compared with point-based baselines, the model identified 6–18% more environmentally suitable area across South Asia, Southeast Asia, and South America, encompassing tens of millions of residents. These findings demonstrate that multiscale spatial context can improve estimates of relative dengue suitability. More broadly, mask-aware convolutional density-ratio estimation provides a flexible framework for mapping environmentally structured pathogens from incomplete, presence-only occurrence data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of traditional infectious-disease risk models, which often rely on incomplete and spatially biased occurrence records. Dengue virus is a significant public health concern due to its environmental and geographic variability.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a spatially disjoint train-test design to evaluate a deep-learning framework for presence-only data. It focused on dengue virus as a global case study, analyzing environmental data across South Asia, Southeast Asia, and South America.
analysis.methods: The model used a deep-learning approach to process gridded environmental patches at local, neighbourhood, and broader landscape scales. It incorporated mask-aware convolutional density-ratio estimation to handle missing raster values and learn the contribution of each spatial scale.
analysis.main_results: The model achieved a Boyce index of 0.971 and an AUC of 0.976 on the held-out test set. It identified 6–18% more environmentally suitable area across South Asia, Southeast Asia, and South America compared to point-based ENM baselines.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that multiscale spatial context can improve estimates of relative dengue suitability. This approach provides a flexible framework for mapping environmentally structured pathogens from incomplete occurrence data.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform more accurate global dengue suitability mapping, aiding in surveillance, risk assessment, and targeted public health interventions in high-risk regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's spatially disjoint train-test design provides moderate confidence in the model's performance. However, the generalizability of the findings may be limited by the specific environmental data used.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a deep-learning framework that improves global dengue suitability mapping by incorporating multiscale spatial context. Traditional models often rely on incomplete and spatially biased occurrence records, making them less effective. The model processes environmental data at local, neighbourhood, and broader landscape scales, learning the contribution of each scale and accommodating missing raster values. It achieved a Boyce index of 0.971 and an AUC of 0.976 on the test set, identifying 6–18% more environmentally suitable areas in South Asia, Southeast Asia, and South America. These findings demonstrate that multiscale spatial representation enhances the accuracy of dengue suitability estimates. The approach offers a flexible framework for mapping pathogens from presence-only data, with potential implications for surveillance and risk assessment. However, the study's spatially disjoint train-test design limits the generalizability of the results, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title_zh: 具有多尺度空间背景的深度学习可改善全球登革热适宜性绘图
source_body_en: Abstract Infectious-disease risk models often rely on occurrence records that are incomplete and spatially biased by surveillance effort, diagnostic access, and outbreak history. Ecological niche modelling (ENM) can identify areas where disease occurrence is environmentally plausible, yet most approaches represent locations using only pointwise covariate values and therefore overlook the surrounding spatial context and rely on presence-only data. Here, we present a deep-learning framework for presence-only data that estimates relative disease suitability by comparing the environmental conditions surrounding reported occurrences with those sampled across the wider study area. The model processes gridded environmental patches at local, neighbourhood, and broader landscape scales, learns the contribution of each scale, and accommodates missing raster values. Using dengue virus as a global case study, we evaluate whether multiscale spatial representation improves upon point-based ENM baselines including random forest and maximum entropy (MaxEnt) under a spatially disjoint train-test design. The model achieved a Boyce index of 0.971 and an AUC of 0.976 on the held-out test set. Learned scale weights and ablation experiments indicated that neighbourhood context contributed most strongly, while local and broader-scale information provided complementary predictive signals. Compared with point-based baselines, the model identified 6–18% more environmentally suitable area across South Asia, Southeast Asia, and South America, encompassing tens of millions of residents. These findings demonstrate that multiscale spatial context can improve estimates of relative dengue suitability. More broadly, mask-aware convolutional density-ratio estimation provides a flexible framework for mapping environmentally structured pathogens from incomplete, presence-only occurrence data.

title: Viral Dynamic Model‐Informed Dose Selection of Mosnodenvir Prophylaxis against DENV‐3 in a Controlled Human Infection Model
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) infection is a significant global health threat. Mosnodenvir (JNJ‐64281802) is a pan‐serotype small molecule antiviral blocking DENV replication. A Phase IIa study (NCT05048875) evaluated the antiviral activity, safety, and pharmacokinetics of mosnodenvir as prophylaxis against DENV‐3 in a controlled human infection model (CHIM). A combined population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) and viral dynamic model (VDM) was developed to estimate the prophylactic effect of mosnodenvir and to inform dose selection. The PopPK model is a two‐compartment model based on plasma pharmacokinetic data from three Phase I studies and Cohort 1 of the Phase IIa study. Mosnodenvir exposure metrics were estimated for participants receiving high, medium, or low doses. A VDM with an immune response compartment adequately described DENV‐3 RNA profiles for placebo participants and was subsequently extended by including a sigmoid E max relationship with average mosnodenvir concentration at steady state ( C avg,ss ) to capture the antiviral effect on virion production rate. Simulations supported daily and weekly mosnodenvir dosing regimens to further characterize the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationship in Cohort 2. Based on the complete Phase IIa study data, the basic reproductive number for DENV‐3 in this CHIM was estimated at 21.7, and the typical C avg,ss required to achieve complete virus eradication was estimated to be 1,410 ng/mL. In conclusion, the combined PopPK and VDM approach effectively informed dose selection and characterized the pharmacokinetic‐antiviral activity relationship, supporting the development of mosnodenvir as a prophylactic treatment for dengue infection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 抗病毒药物 感染仍然是全球主要的健康负担,有效 抗病毒药物 预防的需求尚未得到满足。该研究旨在确定 mosnodenvir 是否可以阻止 DENV-3 在人类中的复制,并使用基于模型的方法确定最佳预防剂量。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项 IIa 期对照人类感染模型 (CHIM) 研究 (NCT05048875) 评估了莫诺登韦对健康志愿者预防 DENV-3 的作用。参与者接受高、中或低剂量的莫诺登韦或安慰剂,并收集药代动力学和病毒动态数据以指导剂量选择。
elements_zh.methods: 使用先前 I 期研究的血浆数据和 CHIM 队列研究 1 建立了两室群体药代动力学 (PopPK) 模型。具有 免疫应答 室的病毒动力学模型 (VDM) 描述了安慰剂参与者中的 DENV-3 RNA 谱,并扩展到包括将 抗病毒药物 效应与平均稳态莫诺登韦浓度 (C avg,ss) 联系起来的 sigmoid E max 关系)。进行模拟来表征 队列研究 2 的药代动力学/药效关系并支持给药方案。
elements_zh.main_results: CHIM 中 DENV-3 的基本繁殖数估计为 21.7,完全根除病毒所需的典型 C avg,ss 为 1,410 ng/mL。对各剂量组的 Mosnodenvir 暴露指标进行了估计,PopPK-VDM 组合方法证明了 抗病毒药物 对病毒粒子生产率的影响。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,整合 PopPK 和 VDM 可以有效地告知剂量选择,并表征药代动力学 - 抗病毒药物 活性关系,代表了登革热 抗病毒药物 开发的一种新的模型知情策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持莫诺登韦作为登革热感染预防药物 抗病毒药物 的潜力,并为未来临床试验中优化 抗病毒药物 剂量提供了框架。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小和使用受控人类感染模型的限制,可能无法完全反映自然登革热 传播 动态。证据强度中等,依赖于基于模型的外推和模拟,而不是直接的临床疗效数据。

title: Dengue fever and chikungunya: prevalence, hematological parameters, and associated factors among febrile patients in eastern Ethiopia: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Dengue fever and chikungunya are emerging arboviral diseases and are becoming major public health threats in tropical and subtropical regions. However, the actual burden and contributing factors are not well studied in Ethiopia. Thus, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of dengue fever and chikungunya and assess the hematological parameters and associated factors among febrile patients in eastern Ethiopia. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Dire Dawa city administration from October to December 2023. Sociodemographic and clinical information of patients were collected using a structured questionnaire and checklist. Hematological parameters were determined using the Mindray BC-3000 Plus automated hematology analyzer. The Kruskal–Wallis test, Spearman correlation test, and logistic regression were used during data analysis. A P-value of < .05 with a 95% confidence interval was considered statistically significant. A total of 576 febrile patients were investigated. The majority of the study participants, 312 (54.2%), were male, and 524 (91%) were rural residents. Nearly 327 (57%) cases were diagnosed with dengue fever, while 73 (13%) cases were for chikungunya. The type of visited healthcare institution (Sabian Comprehensive Hospital, AOR: 8.2 [95% CI: 4.02, 17.3] and Dilchora Referral Hospital, AOR: 2.3 [95% CI: 1.5, 3.7]), urban residence (AOR: 2.3, 95% CI: 1.37–7.7), government employment (AOR: 0.34 [0.12–0.99]), and patients’ previous history of a similar AFI (acute febrile illness) AOR: 3.2 (95% CI: 1.02, 10.3) were significantly associated with empiric arboviral diseases. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了临床诊断的登革热和基孔肯雅热病例的高发生率,以及某些社会人口和制度因素与虫媒病毒疾病之间的显着关联,强调了早期 诊断 的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了 监测 和针对埃塞俄比亚东部虫媒病毒性疾病的针对性干预措施的重要性,特别是考虑到在登革热患者中观察到的血液学异常。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,在没有实验室确认 诊断 感染的情况下依赖临床 诊断 会降低特异性;因此,证据强度中等。

title: The disappearance, and re-emergence of Aedes aegypti in Iran: historical and current status, rising dengue fever threat
abstract: Aedes aegypti is the proven vector of dengue fever, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever. In Iran, the first recorded sighting of Ae. aegypti dates back to 1920 and into the early 1950s. For 70 years, the species was not seen in the country. However, since 2018, reports have confirmed the presence of Ae. aegypti in various regions. It is now established in some areas of the southern provinces, including Hormozgan, Bushehr, and Sistan and Baluchistan. The appearance, disappearance, and subsequent re-emergence of Ae. aegypti in Iran, after a 70-year absence, are attributed to a combination of factors such as historical malaria control, infrastructure, globalization, urbanization, and climate change that is discussed in this study. This study underscores that the re-emergence of Ae. aegypti in Iran necessitates an urgent paradigm shift from reactive chemical-based control toward a proactive, integrated management framework. Ultimately, the long-term mitigation of dengue fever risk depends on the seamless integration of community-based environmental management with advanced biotechnological interventions.

source_records.title: The disappearance, and re-emergence of Aedes aegypti in Iran: historical and current status, rising dengue fever threat.
source_records.abstract: Aedes aegypti is the proven vector of dengue fever, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever. In Iran, the first recorded sighting of Ae. aegypti dates back to 1920 and into the early 1950s. For 70 years, the species was not seen in the country. However, since 2018, reports have confirmed the presence of Ae. aegypti in various regions. It is now established in some areas of the southern provinces, including Hormozgan, Bushehr, and Sistan and Baluchistan. The appearance, disappearance, and subsequent re-emergence of Ae. aegypti in Iran, after a 70-year absence, are attributed to a combination of factors such as historical malaria control, infrastructure, globalization, urbanization, and climate change that is discussed in this study. This study underscores that the re-emergence of Ae. aegypti in Iran necessitates an urgent paradigm shift from reactive chemical-based control toward a proactive, integrated management framework. Ultimately, the long-term mitigation of dengue fever risk depends on the seamless integration of community-based environmental management with advanced biotechnological interventions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates the historical and current status of Aedes aegypti in Iran, focusing on the factors contributing to its re-emergence and the associated threat of dengue fever.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reviews historical records and current reports of Aedes aegypti sightings in Iran, spanning from 1920 to 2018, and identifies regions where the species has re-established itself.
analysis.methods: The study relies on historical data and recent field observations to trace the timeline of Aedes aegypti presence in Iran, analyzing factors such as malaria control, infrastructure development, globalization, urbanization, and climate change.
analysis.main_results: Aedes aegypti was first recorded in Iran between 1920 and the early 1950s, disappeared for 70 years, and has since re-emerged in various regions, including southern provinces like Hormozgan, Bushehr, and Sistan and Baluchistan.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The re-emergence of Aedes aegypti in Iran highlights the need for a paradigm shift in vector control strategies, emphasizing integrated management over reactive chemical approaches.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of monitoring vector populations and implementing proactive measures to mitigate the risk of dengue fever outbreaks in Iran.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on historical and observational data, which may be subject to gaps in record-keeping and limited direct evidence of dengue virus transmission by the re-emerging Aedes aegypti population. Confidence is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the historical and current status of Aedes aegypti in Iran, highlighting its re-emergence after a 70-year absence and the associated threat of dengue fever. The research attributes this re-emergence to factors such as historical malaria control, infrastructure development, globalization, urbanization, and climate change. The findings emphasize the need for a shift from reactive chemical-based control to integrated management strategies to mitigate dengue risk. While the study relies on observational data, it provides a comprehensive overview of the vector's resurgence and its implications for public health. The evidence suggests that the re-emergence of Aedes aegypti in southern provinces necessitates updated surveillance and intervention approaches to prevent dengue outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究调查了伊朗埃及伊蚊的历史和现状,重点关注导致其重新出现的因素以及 登革热 的相关威胁。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了 1920 年至 2018 年伊朗埃及伊蚊目击事件的历史记录和当前报告,并确定了该物种重新定居的地区。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究依靠历史数据和最近的实地观察来追踪埃及伊蚊在伊朗存在的时间线,分析疟疾控制、基础设施发展、全球化、城市化和气候变化等因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 埃及伊蚊于 1920 年至 1950 年代初首次在伊朗出现,消失了 70 年,此后在多个地区重新出现,包括霍尔木兹甘、布什尔、锡斯坦和俾路支斯坦等南部省份。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 埃及伊蚊在伊朗的重新出现凸显了 媒介 控制策略范式转变的必要性,强调对反应性化学方法的综合管理。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了监测 媒介 人群并采取积极措施以减轻伊朗 登革热 暴发 风险的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于历史和观察数据,这些数据可能会受到记录保存方面的空白以及重新出现的埃及伊蚊种群对 登革病毒 传播 传播 的直接证据的影响。信心程度适中。

title: Transmisión vertical de Dengue: Reporte de un caso neonatal en un centro de alta complejidad en Guayaquil, Ecuador.
abstract: Vertical transmission of neonatal dengue presents a diagnostic challenge in hyperendemic areas such as Guayaquil. We report the case of a female neonate, the daughter of a pregnant woman who died from severe peripartum dengue. The patient was admitted with severe perinatal asphyxia, renal injury, and myocardial damage. On the fifth day, she developed fever and a rash, and the diagnosis was confirmed by a positive NS1 antigen test. During the critical phase, she developed hemoconcentration, thrombocytopenia, and pulmonary edema due to capillary leak. Grade 2 intraventricular hemorrhage was also documented. Dynamic fluid management allowed for stabilization without the need for blood products. The patient was discharged in stable condition after 14 days with multidisciplinary follow-up. Publicizing this case raises suspicion of dengue in an underreported age group; timely perinatal detection is crucial to prevent mortality associated with severe complications.

title: Evidence of dengue transmission and a diverse Aedes mosquito virome on the Congo’s Angola border
abstract: Abstract Aedes mosquitoes are widely distributed across the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and are major vectors of dengue (DENV), Zika, chikungunya (CHIKV), and yellow fever (YFV) viruses. While the high burden of malaria in the DRC receives considerable attention, arboviruses remain understudied. In the setting of recent CHIKV and YFV outbreaks in southwestern DRC, we collect Aedes mosquitoes in three areas of Kimpese, DRC, near the Angola border, to investigate their virome. Metagenomic and targeted sequencing of eight randomly selected field mosquito pools, comprising 155 mosquitoes from three collection sites, confirm high-confidence DENV reads and human blood meals in six (75%) and eight (100%) pools, respectively. We find diverse mosquito viromes including other known and putative human and animal viruses. Our findings provide strong evidence of endemic DENV transmission along the DRC-Angola border and illustrate the potential of wild-caught mosquitoes for xenosurveillance of emerging pathogens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue remains understudied in the Democratic Republic of Congo despite the presence of Aedes mosquitoes that transmit it, and recent outbreaks of other arboviruses in the region highlighted a knowledge gap about local dengue transmission dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study collected Aedes mosquitoes in three areas of Kimpese, DRC, near the Angola border, to investigate their virome in the context of recent chikungunya and yellow fever outbreaks.
analysis.methods: Metagenomic and targeted sequencing were performed on eight randomly selected field mosquito pools comprising 155 mosquitoes from three collection sites to identify viral reads and blood meals.
analysis.main_results: High-confidence dengue virus reads were confirmed in six of eight mosquito pools (75%), and human blood meals were detected in all eight pools (100%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as strong evidence of endemic dengue virus transmission along the DRC-Angola border and highlight the utility of wild-caught mosquitoes for xenosurveillance of emerging pathogens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support targeted surveillance and control measures for dengue in southwestern DRC and demonstrate a practical approach for monitoring arboviral activity using mosquito viromes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and reliance on mosquito pools rather than individual-level data, which constrains generalizability and precise risk assessment, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated dengue virus transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo by collecting Aedes mosquitoes near the Angola border following recent chikungunya and yellow fever outbreaks. Using metagenomic and targeted sequencing of eight mosquito pools totaling 155 individuals, the authors detected high-confidence dengue virus reads in 75% of pools and human blood meals in all pools. title_zh: 刚果安哥拉边境存在登革热 传播 和多种伊蚊病毒组的证据
source_body_en: Abstract Aedes mosquitoes are widely distributed across the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and are major vectors of dengue (DENV), Zika, chikungunya (CHIKV), and yellow fever (YFV) viruses. While the high burden of malaria in the DRC receives considerable attention, arboviruses remain understudied. In the setting of recent CHIKV and YFV outbreaks in southwestern DRC, we collect Aedes mosquitoes in three areas of Kimpese, DRC, near the Angola border, to investigate their virome. Metagenomic and targeted sequencing of eight randomly selected field mosquito pools, comprising 155 mosquitoes from three collection sites, confirm high-confidence DENV reads and human blood meals in six (75%) and eight (100%) pools, respectively. We find diverse mosquito viromes including other known and putative human and animal viruses. Our findings provide strong evidence of endemic DENV transmission along the DRC-Angola border and illustrate the potential of wild-caught mosquitoes for xenosurveillance of emerging pathogens.

abstract: Dengue fever remains one of the most rapidly expanding vector-borne diseases worldwide, driven by complex interactions between host, vector, environment, and increasingly, human mobility. Despite significant advances in mathematical epidemiology, existing models often rely on simplifying assumptions that neglect critical transmission pathways, particularly the role of asymptomatic infections and the implicit influence of population movement. In this study, we develop a rigorous host–vector dengue model that incorporates asymptomatic transmission within a mechanistic and analytically tractable framework, providing a foundational step toward mobility-driven epidemiological modeling. We establish the well-posedness of the model by proving positivity, boundedness, and the existence of invariant regions. A comprehensive qualitative analysis is conducted, including the local and global stability of the disease-free equilibrium, with global stability established via Lyapunov methods. Conditions for the existence of endemic equilibria are obtained, revealing the fundamental role of asymptomatic transmission in sustaining disease persistence. To quantify the relative impact of model parameters, a sensitivity analysis of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\mathcal {R}_0$$\end{document} is performed, identifying key drivers of transmission and highlighting the dominant influence of vector-related parameters and asymptomatic infectivity. elements_zh.methods: 我们通过证明正性、有界性和不变区域的存在性来建立模型的适定性。基本再生数 $$\mathcal {R}_0$$ 是使用下一代矩阵方法得出的,并在无症状携带者存在的情况下检查其流行病学解释。进行了全面的定性分析,包括无病平衡的局部和全局稳定性,并通过李雅普诺夫方法建立了全局稳定性。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果强调了在登革热动力学中考虑无症状 传播 的至关重要性,并为未来纳入空间异质性和人类流动性的扩展提供了严格的数学基线。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项工作弥合了经典区室模型和更现实的流行病学环境之间的差距,为在日益相互联系的人群中设计有效的登革热控制策略提供了理论见解和实际意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据并未报告研究设计或样本量的局限性。研究结果的可信度很高,因为该研究提供了严格的数学框架并确定了登革热 传播 的关键驱动因素。

title: Long Short-Term Memory-Based Multivariate Forecasting Model for Dengue: A Case Study in Sri Lanka
abstract: Dengue fever has been a significant health concern in Sri Lanka since the 1960s. The number of cases has drastically increased over the last decade. elements_zh.main_results: 过去十年来,案件数量急剧增加。虽然所有三个模型都表现出相对较好的性能,但 BiLSTM 模型显着优于其他两个模型。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这项研究肯定了使用 LSTM 来预测类似登革热的 媒介 传播疾病,这些疾病的特点是与预测因子之间存在复杂的关系。为了了解过去长短期记忆 (LSTM) 模型的优势,这项具体研究评估了 LSTM 模型的三种变体。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更准确的登革热预测模型提供信息,从而有助于公共卫生规划和干预策略。该研究强调了 LSTM 模型在根据环境因素预测登革热发生方面的潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的具体局限性。证据强度中等,因为该研究侧重于模型性能,而没有解决更广泛的局限性或偏见。

title: Spatio-Temporal Modeling of Dengue in Argentina (2009–2025): Risk Factors, spatial patterns, and implications for prevention planning
abstract: Abstract Background Dengue has expanded markedly in Argentina, with Aedes aegypti now established in temperate provinces and successive epidemics culminating in a record outbreak in 2024. Disentangling large-scale inter-annual climate variability from local environmental and socio-infrastructural conditions is essential for targeted prevention, yet few studies have modelled dengue determinants across Argentina’s heterogeneous transmission zones at national scale. Methods We analysed 817,699 dengue cases reported across 473 departments in northern and central Argentina from 2009 to 2025 using Bayesian hierarchical spatio-temporal models within the integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA) framework. A zero-inflated negative binomial distribution accounted for overdispersion and excess zeros; spatial, temporal and space–time random effects were combined with climatic, environmental and sociodemographic covariates, and predictive performance was assessed through forward-chaining temporal cross-validation. Results Dengue incidence showed strong inter-annual variability, peaking in 2024. El Niño years carried markedly higher risk independent of seasonal climate. Higher current-summer temperature and relative humidity were associated with increased risk, while previous-spring temperature showed a non-linear carry-over relationship with subsequent transmission. Populations living near waste-disposal sites were at greater risk. The model reliably identified high-risk department-years, including the 2024 epidemic, although forecasting outbreak magnitude remained more challenging. Conclusions Large-scale climate variability, seasonal weather and local environmental factors jointly shape dengue transmission in Argentina. Bayesian risk mapping can guide targeted prevention and seasonal early-warning systems, particularly along the expanding southern transmission frontier.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 登革热在阿根廷已显着蔓延,埃及伊蚊现已在温带省份定居,连续的流行病最终在 2024 年达到创纪录的 暴发。将大规模的年际气候变化与当地环境和社会基础设施条件分开对于有针对性的预防至关重要,但很少有研究在全国范围内对阿根廷异质 传播 区域的登革热决定因素进行建模。方法 我们使用综合嵌套拉普拉斯近似 (INLA) 框架内的贝叶斯分层时空模型分析了 2009 年至 2025 年阿根廷北部和中部 473 个省份报告的 817,699 例登革热病例。零膨胀负二项分布解释了过度分散和过多的零;将空间、时间和时空随机效应与气候、环境和社会人口学协变量相结合,并通过前向链时间交叉验证评估预测性能。结果 登革热 发病率 显示出强烈的年际变化,在 2024 年达到顶峰。厄尔尼诺年份的风险明显较高,与季节气候无关。当前夏季较高的温度和相对湿度与风险增加相关,而前春季温度与随后的 传播 呈非线性结转关系。居住在废物处理场附近的人群面临的风险更大。该模型可靠地识别了高风险部门年份,包括 2024 年的流行病,尽管预测 暴发 的严重程度仍然更具挑战性。结论 大规模气候变率、季节性天气和当地环境因素共同影响了阿根廷登革热 传播。贝叶斯风险图可以指导有针对性的预防和季节性预警系统,特别是在不断扩大的南部 传播 边境地区。

title: Perception and knowledge of the population about dengue fever in a municipality in Northeast of Brazil
abstract: Objective: to evaluate knowledge, habits, and participation in educational activities on dengue among residents of the municipality of Lago do Junco, Maranhão, Brazil. Methodology: this is an observational, cross-sectional study conducted with 264 individuals over 18 years of age, randomly selected. A structured questionnaire was applied, including sociodemographic variables and questions related to the etiological agent, transmission, symptoms, treatment, prevention, and household practices. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and the Chi-square test, with a significance level of 5%. Results: a total of 264 individuals were interviewed, of whom 62.1% were female, 37.0% were aged between 35 and 59 years, and 26.1% had completed high school. Most participants demonstrated satisfactory knowledge about dengue: 91.7% correctly recognized the main signs and symptoms, 80.3% adequately identified prevention methods, and 64.0% correctly indicated transmission through mosquito bites. However, 59.1% reported the presence of water-holding containers in their households, favoring vector proliferation. In addition, 54.2% reported having participated in educational activities. A statistically significant association was observed between higher education level and greater knowledge about the disease (p < 0.05). Conclusion: although the population's knowledge is satisfactory, risky household practices still persist. Therefore, it is necessary to expand and strengthen continuous educational actions, especially targeting more vulnerable groups, aiming to reduce risk behaviors and effectively control dengue in the municipality.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the knowledge, habits, and participation in educational activities regarding dengue fever among residents of Lago do Junco, Maranhão, Brazil. It found that most participants had satisfactory knowledge about dengue, including its symptoms, prevention methods, and transmission. However, a significant proportion reported the presence of water-holding containers in their households, which can promote vector proliferation. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估巴西马拉尼昂州 Lago do Junco 市居民对登革热教育活动的知识、习惯和参与情况。这项研究的动机是需要了解公众对 登革热 的看法和认识,登革热 是该地区的一个重大公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项观察性横断面研究,研究对象为 264 名 18 岁以上的个体,这些个体是从巴西马拉尼昂州 Lago do Junco 市随机抽取的。该研究于2024年至2025年间进行。
elements_zh.methods: 采用结构化调查问卷,包括社会人口统计学变量以及与病因、传播、症状、治疗、预防和家庭实践相关的问题。使用描述性统计和卡方检验对数据进行分析,显着性水平为5%。
elements_zh.main_results: 共有 264 人接受采访,其中 62.1% 为女性,37.0% 年龄在 35 岁至 59 岁之间,26.1% 完成高中学业。大多数参与者对登革热的了解令人满意:91.7% 的人正确识别了主要体征和症状,80.3% 的人充分识别了预防方法,64.0% 的人通过蚊虫叮咬正确指示了 传播。然而,59.1% 的人表示家里有盛水的容器,这有利于 媒介 的扩散。此外,54.2%的人表示曾参加过教育活动。较高的教育水平与对该疾病的更多了解之间存在统计学上显着的关联(p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,尽管人们的知识水平令人满意,但危险的家庭做法仍然存在。这项研究为教育水平与登革热知识之间的关系提供了新颖的见解,强调了有针对性的教育干预措施的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调教育活动的重要性来为公共卫生战略提供信息,以提高知识并改变与登革热预防相关的危险行为。这有助于制定更有效的基于社区的干预措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,不允许进行因果推断。由于依赖自我报告的数据和潜在的回忆偏差,证据的强度中等。

title: Clinical and Biochemical Characteristics of Dengue Fever and Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever During the 2024 Dengue Outbreak
abstract: Background: Dengue is a vector-borne viral infection that poses a significant public health threat in tropical and subtropical regions, ranging from mild fever to severe forms like DHF and DSS. Gender and platelet count are thought to influence disease severity, but their roles remain unclear. Objective: This study aims to explore the demographic, clinical, and laboratory characteristics of dengue patients, focusing on gender differences and platelet count’s association. Methodology: This was a prospective study carried out in the Department of Virology in NILMRC, Dhaka, Bangladesh from July to November 2024. The study population comprised confirmed dengue patients admitted to the Medicine Ward of AMZ Hospital during the study period, as well as outdoor patients from NILMRC, who met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Serology and RT PCR were performed. Results: 57.9% were male and 42.1% were female, with a higher prevalence of dengue among males. The majority of patients were in the 16-25 (30.1%) and 26-35 (29.5%) age groups. Gender differences were observed in clinical features: males more frequently reported cough, headache, myalgia, fatigue, joint pain, and low platelet count, while females had a higher incidence of rash and nausea/vomiting. A higher proportion of males (8.2%) experienced severe complications like DHF/DSS.84.2% having platelet counts >100,000 cells/μL. Elevated liver enzymes (AST and ALT) were observed in 42.5% and 37% of patients, respectively. DENV-2 was the predominant serotype (61%). Lower platelet counts (≤100,000 cells/μL) were associated with higher incidences of severe complications, elevated AST and ALT levels, and hematocrit rise >20%. Conclusion: This study highlights significant gender differences in the clinical presentation and severity of dengue, with males more frequently experiencing musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and severe complications like DHF and DSS. Platelet count emerged as a key marker for predicting severe outcomes. Journal of Monno Medical College December, 2025;11(2):113-120

title: Digital Surveillance for Vector Control: Deployment and Evaluation of a Web-Based Dengue Monitoring System in Colombia
abstract: Abstract Background Digital technologies are increasingly used in public health to improve data management and strengthen disease-control operations. This study describes the design, development, and field testing of a web-based software system—Digital Surveillance of Vector Control (DSVC)—to monitor and evaluate vector control programs. The system was deployed during a large-scale intervention using a novel larvicidal/adulticidal protective coating (PC) applied to domestic water containers, the main larval habitat of dengue-transmitting Aedes mosquitoes in many tropical cities. A field study was conducted in Cúcuta and Los Patios, Colombia, to assess the potential of DSVC to reduce data processing time, improve accuracy, and support timely decision-making. Methodology: DSVC was developed to optimize data processing and monitoring vector control activities. It was tested under real operational conditions by integrating data collected by community volunteers during visits to approximately 8,000 households. Two data-collection methods were compared: traditional paper forms and the Epicollect5 mobile application. The principal investigator monitored real-time data processing, analysis, and visualization through DSVC. In-depth interviews with municipal data management engineers assessed the system’s potential integration into local health services. Focus group discussions with community volunteers and vector control technicians explored acceptance, usability, and perceived advantages and limitations of Epicollect5. Results DSVC reduced data processing time and improved accuracy compared to paper-based workflows. The system efficiently managed large data volumes and enabled rapid aggregation and visualization of data. Municipal vector control technicians reported that DSVC met key requirements for monitoring vector control activities. Interviews and focus groups indicated positive acceptance of digital tools, highlighting their potential for adoption in routine programs. Epicollect5 facilitated integration of paper-based and digital data, reduced errors, and accelerated data capture. However, fieldwork revealed risks of device theft and persistent preference for paper forms in some neighborhoods. Conclusion DSVC and Epicollect5 enhanced the efficiency of data collection and analysis, enabling faster and more targeted responses. Digital tools represent a significant advancement for optimizing vector control programs. Municipal departments identified the system’s potential for future integration, pending administrative decisions. User acceptance, operational feasibility, and clear workflows are essential for maximizing the impact of digital tools in vector control.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 数字技术越来越多地应用于公共卫生领域,以改善数据管理并加强疾病控制行动。本研究描述了基于网络的软件系统(媒介 Control (DSVC) 的数字 监测)的设计、开发和现场测试,以监视和评估 媒介 控制程序。该系统是在大规模干预期间部署的,使用一种新型杀幼虫/杀成虫保护涂层(PC)应用于家用水容器,这是许多热带城市传播登革热的伊蚊的主要幼虫栖息地。在哥伦比亚库库塔和洛斯帕蒂奥斯进行了一项实地研究,以评估 DSVC 在减少数据处理时间、提高准确性和支持及时决策方面的潜力。方法:DSVC 的开发是为了优化数据处理和监控 媒介 控制活动。该系统通过整合社区志愿者走访约 8,000 个家庭期间收集的数据,在实际操作条件下进行了测试。比较了两种数据收集方法:传统纸质表格和 Epicollect5 移动应用程序。首席研究员通过 DSVC 监控实时数据处理、分析和可视化。对市政数据管理工程师的深入采访评估了该系统融入当地卫生服务的潜力。与社区志愿者和 媒介 控制技术人员进行的焦点小组讨论探讨了 Epicollect5 的接受度、可用性以及感知的优点和局限性。结果 与纸质工作流程相比,DSVC 减少了数据处理时间并提高了准确性。该系统有效管理大量数据,并实现数据的快速聚合和可视化。市政 媒介 控制技术人员报告称,DSVC 满足监测 媒介 控制活动的关键要求。访谈和焦点小组表明对数字工具的积极接受,强调了它们在常规项目中采用的潜力。Epicollect5 促进了纸质数据和数字数据的集成,减少了错误并加速了数据捕获。然而,实地调查显示,一些社区存在设备被盗的风险以及对纸质表格的持续偏好。结论 DSVC 和 Epicollect5 提高了数据收集和分析的效率,从而实现更快、更有针对性的响应。数字工具代表了优化 媒介 控制程序的重大进步。市政部门确定了该系统未来整合的潜力,有待行政决策。用户接受度、操作可行性和清晰的工作流程对于最大化 媒介 控制中数字工具的影响至关重要。

title: Urban Hyperendemicity and Emerging Coastal Per-Capita Risk of Dengue in Bangladesh, 2021-2025: A Nationwide Spatiotemporal Ecological Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue has shifted from Dhaka-centric to nationwide in Bangladesh. AIM: To quantify spatiotemporal patterns and identify high-risk clusters across all 64 districts from 2021 to 2025, and, extending previous reports with data from 2025, this study aims to observe an ongoing shift in per-capita risk hotspots. METHODS: Retrospective ecological study of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) aggregate yearly data on suspected and laboratory-confirmed dengue admissions (n = 637,626 cases). Incidence per 100,000 population was calculated using 2022 census projections with 1.12% annual growth. Global (Moran's I) and local (Getis-Ord Gi∗) spatial autocorrelation and prospective space-time scan statistics (SaTScan) were applied. RESULTS: National incidence: 76.4/100,000/year. 2025 rate-adjusted Moran's I = 0.328 (p = 0.001). Raw-case hotspots: Greater Dhaka; population-adjusted hotspots: Jhalokathi, Barguna (coastal). High-rate space-time cluster (2024-2025): Dhaka, Manikganj (RR = 3.13, p = 0.001). Dhaka O/E = 4.31 (RR = 6.38). Two low-rate clusters (north, southeast). CONCLUSION: Urban hyperendemicity, characterized by a high case volume, coupled with the emerging coastal per-capita risk, necessitates tailored interventions. Intensive vector control is essential in Dhaka, while early-warning surveillance should be implemented in coastal districts.

The research highlights urban hyperendemicity and emerging coastal risk, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions. title_zh: 孟加拉国城市高流行和新兴沿海人均登革热风险,2021-2025 年:全国时空生态分析。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Dengue has shifted from Dhaka-centric to nationwide in Bangladesh. AIM: To quantify spatiotemporal patterns and identify high-risk clusters across all 64 districts from 2021 to 2025, and, extending previous reports with data from 2025, this study aims to observe an ongoing shift in per-capita risk hotspots. METHODS: Retrospective ecological study of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) aggregate yearly data on suspected and laboratory-confirmed dengue admissions (n = 637,626 cases). Incidence per 100,000 population was calculated using 2022 census projections with 1.12% annual growth. Global (Moran's I) and local (Getis-Ord Gi∗) spatial autocorrelation and prospective space-time scan statistics (SaTScan) were applied. RESULTS: National incidence: 76.4/100,000/year. 2025 rate-adjusted Moran's I = 0.328 (p = 0.001). Raw-case hotspots: Greater Dhaka; population-adjusted hotspots: Jhalokathi, Barguna (coastal). High-rate space-time cluster (2024-2025): Dhaka, Manikganj (RR = 3.13, p = 0.001). Dhaka O/E = 4.31 (RR = 6.38). Two low-rate clusters (north, southeast). CONCLUSION: Urban hyperendemicity, characterized by a high case volume, coupled with the emerging coastal per-capita risk, necessitates tailored interventions. Intensive vector control is essential in Dhaka, while early-warning surveillance should be implemented in coastal districts.

title: Editorial: Emerging arboviruses in the Americas: epidemiology, public health impact, and future preparedness
abstract: The burden of arboviral diseases is intensifying rather than stabilizing. Dengue continues to reach unprecedented levels across the Americas, while geospatial clustering across Brazilian municipalities in 2024 highlights substantial fine-scale heterogeneity in transmission, underscoring the need for targeted and locally tailored control measures. This challenge is not confined to endemic regions: screening of blood donors in Shenzhen, China, illustrates how arboviruses can silently move through global travel networks and establish risks far beyond their traditional areas of circulation. Chikungunya provides a compelling example of the recurring epidemic waves that may characterize the coming decades. Twenty years after the devastating 2005-2006 epidemic, Réunion Island experienced another major outbreak in 2025. Our analysis estimated roughly 208 excess deaths among older adults during a three-month period; the age-specific excess mortality rate reached 145.3 per 100,000 (95% CI: 125.5-165.0) with a case fatality rate (CFR) of 2.4%, substantially exceeding officially reported fatalities (1). National-level analyses from Brazil similarly demonstrate a significant burden of hospitalization and mortality associated with chikungunya infection (2). Together, these findings suggest that the true impact of chikungunya has been consistently underestimated. The Réunion experience serves as a warning for the Americas, where more than a decade has passed since the virus became established following its introduction in 2014-2015. Conditions favorable for a comparable resurgence may already be in place. A recurring lesson emerges across arboviral diseases: surveillance systems based primarily on laboratory-confirmed cases frequently underestimate the true burden of infection and disease.Vectors remain central to this intensification. Several contributions in this Research Topic highlight the increasingly complex ecological and epidemiological factors shaping arboviral transmission. Studies range from the growing prevalence of pyrethroid resistance (kdr) mutations in Aedes aegypti populations in northeastern Argentina-threatening the long-term effectiveness of conventional vector control-to transcriptomic investigations of Wolbachia in this mosquito species, which reveal promising avenues for biological control interventions. Human factors also contribute substantially. A study assessing knowledge and attitudes toward chikungunya among healthcare workers in Chengdu, China, identified important awareness gaps that may delay recognition and diagnosis. Against this backdrop, climate variability-including the prospect of future El Niño events-is likely to amplify transmission risks and contribute to increasingly severe dengue seasons, alongside renewed activity of chikungunya, yellow fever, and Oropouche virus.The most concerning trend emerging from this collection is the continued geographic and ecological expansion of arboviruses. Yellow fever activity has intensified markedly, with 2025 recording the highest annual case count since 2020 and transmission extending into areas without a historical record of disease occurrence, including São Paulo State (3). Genomic investigation demonstrates the virus re-emerging across forest and periurban environments while advancing along forest edges toward densely populated, and often under-vaccinated, communities (4). Importantly, the prospect of yellow fever re-urbanization is no longer merely theoretical. Yellow fever virus has been detected and isolated from Aedes albopictus in an urban green area of São Paulo State (5). At the same time, Aedes vittatus-first recorded in the Americas in the Dominican Republic in 2019 (6) and now expanding across both insular and continental Caribbean regions-represents another potential bridge vector connecting sylvatic and urban transmission cycles (7). In this context, suboptimal vaccination coverage in newly affected areas remains the most important modifiable vulnerability.Oropouche virus presents a parallel narrative of geographic expansion. Once considered largely confined to the Amazon Basin, the virus has increasingly demonstrated its capacity to spread beyond its historical range. Surveillance efforts in wild birds at rehabilitation centers in Florida are now evaluating whether competent vertebrate hosts exist in North America, an increasingly relevant question given the growing number of imported human infections. Within Brazil, genomic surveillance recently documented the first imported case in Rio Grande do Sul, alongside enzootic circulation of Culicoides paraensis, signaling a tangible outbreak risk in one of the southernmost regions of the country (8). Additional studies further emphasize the importance of vigilance at the margins of known transmission zones. The detection of alphavirus circulation in Costa Rica, together with the description of the first case of West Nile virus meningoencephalitis in southwest Michigan, illustrates how arboviruses continue to establish themselves in new ecological settings, host populations, and vulnerable patient groups. Early recognition of such transitions remains critical for effective public health response.As arboviruses expand into new territories, their clinical spectrum is also being redefined. Oropouche virus, historically regarded as a self-limiting febrile illness, has increasingly emerged as a pathogen capable of causing severe neurological disease and adverse congenital outcomes. Experimental evidence demonstrating enhanced virulence and neuroinvasive capacity of contemporary Oropouche virus strains in the AG129 mouse model provides biological support for these observations. Clinical reports describing neurological manifestations-including Guillain-Barré syndrome accompanied by bilateral visual impairment associated with an emerging reassortant lineage in Ceará ( 9)-further expand the recognized disease phenotype. The possibility of congenital Oropouche syndrome has also gained increasing attention. A hypothesis initially raised within this Research Topic has since been reinforced by reports of newborns presenting with microcephaly following maternal infection in Brazil (10). These findings suggest that the public health implications of Oropouche virus may be substantially broader than previously appreciated. More broadly, mechanistic studies included in this collection contribute valuable insights into arboviral pathogenesis. For example, evidence demonstrating that disruption of a glycosylation site in the Zika virus envelope protein attenuates viral replication provides important clues regarding determinants of flaviviral virulence and identifies potential targets for future intervention strategies.Chikungunya reinforces this theme from a different perspective. Rather than revealing a new clinical syndrome, recent evidence highlights a long-recognized but consistently underreported outcome: mortality. The findings from Réunion Island and Brazil clearly indicate that chikungunya-associated deaths remain substantially underestimated by conventional surveillance systems (1,2).Several contributions in this Research Topic point toward the strategies needed to address future arboviral threats. Reviews examining current and emerging vector-borne disease risks, together with analyses of knowledge gaps surrounding Caribbean arboviral vectors, collectively support the adoption of integrated One Health approaches that recognize the interconnected roles of humans, animals, vectors, and the environment. As recently emphasized, closing both geographical and methodological gaps in arbovirus surveillance is essential for strengthening preparedness in an era of accelerating environmental change (11). Because case-based surveillance consistently underestimates the true burden of disease, complementary approaches are urgently needed. These include excess-mortality analyses and syndromic surveillance to identify otherwise unrecognized fatalities; integrated entomological and virological surveillance; monitoring of non-human primate mortality as an early warning system for yellow fever circulation; blood-bank screening as a sentinel tool for silent transmission; and minimally invasive tissue sampling to improve the investigation of arboviral deaths, an approach shown to be broadly acceptable in Brazil (12). These surveillance efforts must be accompanied by strengthened vaccination strategies. For yellow fever, as urgently called for by PAHO (3), vaccination coverage must be expanded across all populations exposed to sylvatic and rural transmission settings and increased until it attains at least the population-level protective threshold capable of preventing re-urbanization in newly affected areas. Likewise, broader implementation of available vaccines against dengue and chikungunya will be essential to reduce future disease burden. Together, enhanced surveillance, improved diagnostics, expanded vaccination, strengthened postmortem investigations, and timely public health interventions constitute the foundation of effective preparedness. Emerging arboviruses in the Americas-and increasingly worldwide-do not represent a single problem with a single solution. Rather, they comprise a complex and evolving constellation of threats that require tailored responses. Recognizing the distinct epidemiological, ecological, and clinical dimensions of each risk is the first step toward building the preparedness that the region urgently needs.

Dengue continues to reach unprecedented levels across the Americas, while geospatial clustering across Brazilian municipalities in 2024 highlights substantial fine-scale heterogeneity in transmission, underscoring the need for targeted and locally tailored control measures. This challenge is not confined to endemic regions: screening of blood donors in Shenzhen, China, illustrates how arboviruses can silently move through global travel networks and establish risks far beyond their traditional areas of circulation. Chikungunya provides a compelling example of the recurring epidemic waves that may characterize the coming decades. Twenty years after the devastating 2005-2006 epidemic, Réunion Island experienced another major outbreak in 2025. Our analysis estimated roughly 208 excess deaths among older adults during a three-month period; the age-specific excess mortality rate reached 145.3 per 100,000 (95% CI: 125.5-165.0) with a case fatality rate (CFR) of 2.4%, substantially exceeding officially reported fatalities (1). National-level analyses from Brazil similarly demonstrate a significant burden of hospitalization and mortality associated with chikungunya infection (2). Together, these findings suggest that the true impact of chikungunya has been consistently underestimated. The Réunion experience serves as a warning for the Americas, where more than a decade has passed since the virus became established following its introduction in 2014-2015. Conditions favorable for a comparable resurgence may already be in place. A recurring lesson emerges across arboviral diseases: surveillance systems based primarily on laboratory-confirmed cases frequently underestimate the true burden of infection and disease.Vectors remain central to this intensification. Several contributions in this Research Topic highlight the increasingly complex ecological and epidemiological factors shaping arboviral transmission. Studies range from the growing prevalence of pyrethroid resistance (kdr) mutations in Aedes aegypti populations in northeastern Argentina-threatening the long-term effectiveness of conventional vector control-to transcriptomic investigations of Wolbachia in this mosquito species, which reveal promising avenues for biological control interventions. Human factors also contribute substantially. A study assessing knowledge and attitudes toward chikungunya among healthcare workers in Chengdu, China, identified important awareness gaps that may delay recognition and diagnosis. Against this backdrop, climate variability-including the prospect of future El Niño events-is likely to amplify transmission risks and contribute to increasingly severe dengue seasons, alongside renewed activity of chikungunya, yellow fever, and Oropouche virus.The most concerning trend emerging from this collection is the continued geographic and ecological expansion of arboviruses. Yellow fever activity has intensified markedly, with 2025 recording the highest annual case count since 2020 and transmission extending into areas without a historical record of disease occurrence, including São Paulo State (3). Genomic investigation demonstrates the virus re-emerging across forest and periurban environments while advancing along forest edges toward densely populated, and often under-vaccinated, communities (4). Importantly, the prospect of yellow fever re-urbanization is no longer merely theoretical. Yellow fever virus has been detected and isolated from Aedes albopictus in an urban green area of São Paulo State (5). At the same time, Aedes vittatus-first recorded in the Americas in the Dominican Republic in 2019 (6) and now expanding across both insular and continental Caribbean regions-represents another potential bridge vector connecting sylvatic and urban transmission cycles (7). In this context, suboptimal vaccination coverage in newly affected areas remains the most important modifiable vulnerability.Oropouche virus presents a parallel narrative of geographic expansion. Once considered largely confined to the Amazon Basin, the virus has increasingly demonstrated its capacity to spread beyond its historical range. Surveillance efforts in wild birds at rehabilitation centers in Florida are now evaluating whether competent vertebrate hosts exist in North America, an increasingly relevant question given the growing number of imported human infections. Within Brazil, genomic surveillance recently documented the first imported case in Rio Grande do Sul, alongside enzootic circulation of Culicoides paraensis, signaling a tangible outbreak risk in one of the southernmost regions of the country (8). Additional studies further emphasize the importance of vigilance at the margins of known transmission zones. The detection of alphavirus circulation in Costa Rica, together with the description of the first case of West Nile virus meningoencephalitis in southwest Michigan, illustrates how arboviruses continue to establish themselves in new ecological settings, host populations, and vulnerable patient groups. Early recognition of such transitions remains critical for effective public health response.As arboviruses expand into new territories, their clinical spectrum is also being redefined. Oropouche virus, historically regarded as a self-limiting febrile illness, has increasingly emerged as a pathogen capable of causing severe neurological disease and adverse congenital outcomes. Experimental evidence demonstrating enhanced virulence and neuroinvasive capacity of contemporary Oropouche virus strains in the AG129 mouse model provides biological support for these observations. Clinical reports describing neurological manifestations-including Guillain-Barré syndrome accompanied by bilateral visual impairment associated with an emerging reassortant lineage in Ceará ( 9)-further expand the recognized disease phenotype. The possibility of congenital Oropouche syndrome has also gained increasing attention. A hypothesis initially raised within this Research Topic has since been reinforced by reports of newborns presenting with microcephaly following maternal infection in Brazil (10). These findings suggest that the public health implications of Oropouche virus may be substantially broader than previously appreciated. More broadly, mechanistic studies included in this collection contribute valuable insights into arboviral pathogenesis. For example, evidence demonstrating that disruption of a glycosylation site in the Zika virus envelope protein attenuates viral replication provides important clues regarding determinants of flaviviral virulence and identifies potential targets for future intervention strategies.Chikungunya reinforces this theme from a different perspective. Rather than revealing a new clinical syndrome, recent evidence highlights a long-recognized but consistently underreported outcome: mortality. The findings from Réunion Island and Brazil clearly indicate that chikungunya-associated deaths remain substantially underestimated by conventional surveillance systems (1,2).Several contributions in this Research Topic point toward the strategies needed to address future arboviral threats. Reviews examining current and emerging vector-borne disease risks, together with analyses of knowledge gaps surrounding Caribbean arboviral vectors, collectively support the adoption of integrated One Health approaches that recognize the interconnected roles of humans, animals, vectors, and the environment. As recently emphasized, closing both geographical and methodological gaps in arbovirus surveillance is essential for strengthening preparedness in an era of accelerating environmental change (11). Because case-based surveillance consistently underestimates the true burden of disease, complementary approaches are urgently needed. These include excess-mortality analyses and syndromic surveillance to identify otherwise unrecognized fatalities; integrated entomological and virological surveillance; monitoring of non-human primate mortality as an early warning system for yellow fever circulation; blood-bank screening as a sentinel tool for silent transmission; and minimally invasive tissue sampling to improve the investigation of arboviral deaths, an approach shown to be broadly acceptable in Brazil (12). These surveillance efforts must be accompanied by strengthened vaccination strategies. For yellow fever, as urgently called for by PAHO (3), vaccination coverage must be expanded across all populations exposed to sylvatic and rural transmission settings and increased until it attains at least the population-level protective threshold capable of preventing re-urbanization in newly affected areas. Likewise, broader implementation of available vaccines against dengue and chikungunya will be essential to reduce future disease burden. Together, enhanced surveillance, improved diagnostics, expanded vaccination, strengthened postmortem investigations, and timely public health interventions constitute the foundation of effective preparedness. Emerging arboviruses in the Americas-and increasingly worldwide-do not represent a single problem with a single solution. Rather, they comprise a complex and evolving constellation of threats that require tailored responses. Recognizing the distinct epidemiological, ecological, and clinical dimensions of each risk is the first step toward building the preparedness that the region urgently needs.
title_original: Editorial: Emerging arboviruses in the Americas: epidemiology, public health impact, and future preparedness

analysis.research_question_and_background: The editorial highlights the intensifying global burden of arboviral diseases, particularly dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and Oropouche virus, which are expanding geographically and ecologically beyond traditional endemic regions. It emphasizes the need to address persistent knowledge gaps regarding underestimated disease burden and the drivers of transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The editorial synthesizes findings from multiple studies and surveillance reports across the Americas and globally, focusing on arboviral diseases and their vectors. It integrates data from national-level analyses, genomic investigations, and ecological studies without specifying a single study design or population.
analysis.methods: The editorial relies on national surveillance data, genomic sequencing, entomological surveys, and ecological modeling to assess arboviral transmission dynamics and disease burden. It also incorporates studies on vector competence, resistance mutations, and human behavioral factors influencing transmission.
analysis.main_results: The editorial reports that dengue transmission in Brazil shows substantial fine-scale heterogeneity, with geospatial clustering across municipalities in 2024. It also notes that chikungunya has caused recurring epidemic waves, including a major outbreak in Réunion Island in 2025 with an estimated 208 excess deaths among older adults and a case fatality rate of 2.4%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that the true burden of arboviral diseases, particularly chikungunya, has been consistently underestimated due to underreporting in surveillance systems. They highlight the novelty of documenting the expansion of yellow fever into new regions, including São Paulo State, and the detection of yellow fever virus in Aedes albopictus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the urgent need for improved surveillance, targeted vector control, and enhanced vaccination coverage to mitigate the expanding threat of arboviral diseases. They also emphasize the importance of addressing suboptimal vaccination coverage and ecological factors driving transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The editorial is based on a synthesis of diverse studies and surveillance reports, which may introduce variability in data quality and comparability. The evidence strength is moderate, as it relies on aggregated data and modeling rather than controlled studies, and some findings are derived from abstracts or preliminary reports.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial examines the intensifying burden and geographic expansion of arboviral diseases, particularly dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and Oropouche virus, across the Americas and globally. It highlights the underestimation of disease burden due to surveillance limitations and the role of ecological and human factors in driving transmission. Key findings include substantial fine-scale heterogeneity in dengue transmission in Brazil, recurring chikungunya epidemic waves with significant mortality, and the expansion of yellow fever into new regions, including São Paulo State. The authors emphasize the need for improved surveillance, targeted vector control, and vaccination strategies to address these growing public health threats.

title: Evaluating the Statistical Significance of Grid Search Optimization in Support Vector Regression for Dengue Forecasting Using Nested Time-Series Cross-Validation
abstract: Background Support Vector Regression (SVR) is widely employed for epidemic forecasting because kernel methods effectively model nonlinear, multivariate, and lagged climate-disease relationships. While practitioners routinely apply exhaustive grid-search hyperparameter optimization, whether such computationally expensive tuning produces statistically significant predictive enhancements under strict, leakage-free time-series validation remains an open empirical question. Objective To rigorously evaluate the statistical significance and practical utility of grid-search hyperparameter optimization for SVR-based weekly dengue case forecasting. Methods Utilizing the publicly available DengAI benchmark for San Juan, Puerto Rico, and Iquitos, Peru, from 1990 to 2013 (N = 1,872 city-weeks), this study constructs a strictly leakage-free pipeline. This pipeline incorporates median imputation, training-exclusive Z-score outlier mitigation, standardization, and Principal Component Analysis. We compared the default SVR configuration against a grid-tuned SVR optimized over the regularization constant, epsilon-insensitive tube, and kernel coefficient. Three validation protocols were applied: a chronological 80:20 hold-out, rolling-origin time-series cross-validation, and nested time-series cross-validation utilizing five outer folds. Statistical inference relied on paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests applied to outer-fold errors, complemented by Cohen’s dz effect sizes, percentile-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and Holm-Bonferroni multiplicity correction. Methodological robustness was examined by systematically varying the number of retained principal components. Results On the chronological hold-out evaluation, the grid search reduced the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by a marginal 0.30% in Iquitos and 0.59% in San Juan. Under nested cross-validation, the mean difference in MAE between the tuned and default models demonstrated a 0.024-case reduction in Iquitos (p = 1.0000) and a 0.494-case increase in San Juan (p = 0.1875). Neither result achieved statistical significance following multiplicity correction. Furthermore, the selected hyperparameters exhibited severe instability across the outer validation folds, particularly for San Juan. The optimization process also incurred an additional 11.48 seconds and 14.80 seconds of computational wall-clock overhead per city, respectively, without delivering a corresponding accuracy benefit. Conclusion Within the context of the DengAI benchmark and a robust leakage-free preprocessing pipeline, the default SVR configuration is statistically indistinguishable from its grid-tuned counterpart. These findings suggest that hyperparameter optimization in epidemic forecasting should not be executed automatically. Instead, it must be strategically guided by a pre-registered Smallest Effect Size of Interest and an explicit computational stopping rule. The comprehensive methodological framework presented in this study offers a potentially transferable framework for evaluating optimization utility in other low-fold time-series forecasting domains.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the statistical significance of grid search optimization in Support Vector Regression (SVR) for dengue forecasting using nested time-series cross-validation. The research aimed to determine whether computationally expensive hyperparameter tuning improves predictive accuracy in a leakage-free setting. The study used data from San Juan, Puerto Rico, and Iquitos, Peru, from 1990 to 2013, applying a preprocessing pipeline with median imputation, Z-score outlier mitigation, standardization, and Principal Component Analysis. The grid-tuned SVR was compared against the default configuration using three validation protocols. The results showed marginal improvements in MAE for both cities, but these did not achieve statistical significance after multiplicity correction. The findings suggest that hyperparameter optimization should not be automated in epidemic forecasting and must be guided by pre-registered criteria. The study highlights the need for methodological frameworks to assess optimization utility in time-series forecasting, particularly in low-fold settings. However, the optimization process introduced significant computational overhead without corresponding accuracy gains, raising concerns about its practical utility.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景支持 媒介 回归 (SVR) 广泛用于流行病预测,因为核方法可以有效地模拟非线性、多变量和滞后的气候与疾病关系。虽然从业者通常应用详尽的网格搜索超参数优化,但这种计算成本高昂的调整是否在严格、无泄漏的时间序列验证下产生统计上显着的预测增强仍然是一个悬而未决的经验问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究利用 1990 年至 2013 年(N = 1,872 个城市周)波多黎各圣胡安和秘鲁伊基托斯公开的 DengAI 基准构建了一条严格无泄漏的管道。该管道包含中值插补、训练专用的 Z 分数异常值缓解、标准化和主成分分析。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究将默认 SVR 配置与针对正则化常数、ε 不敏感管和核系数进行优化的网格调整 SVR 进行了比较。应用了三种验证协议:时间顺序 80:20 保留、滚动源时间序列交叉验证以及利用五个外折叠的嵌套时间序列交叉验证。统计推断依赖于应用于外折叠误差的成对 Wilcoxon 符号秩检验,并辅以 Cohen 的 dz 效应大小、百分位引导 95% 置信区间和 Holm-Bonferroni 多重校正。
elements_zh.main_results: 在按时间顺序保留的评估中,网格搜索将伊基托斯的平均绝对误差 (MAE) 减少了 0.30%,在圣胡安减少了 0.59%。在嵌套交叉验证下,调整模型和默认模型之间的 MAE 平均差异表明,伊基托斯的案例减少了 0.024 个案例(p = 1.0000),而圣胡安的案例增加了 0.494 个案例(p = 0.1875)。经过多重校正后,这两个结果均未达到统计显着性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,流行病预测中的超参数优化不应自动执行。相反,它必须由预先注册的最小利益效应大小和明确的计算停止规则进行战略指导。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究提出的综合方法框架为评估其他低倍时间序列预测领域的优化效用提供了一个潜在的可移植框架。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 优化过程分别导致每个城市额外增加 11.48 秒和 14.80 秒的计算挂钟开销,但没有带来相应的准确性优势。所选的超参数在外部验证折叠中表现出严重的不稳定,特别是对于圣胡安。

abstract_zh: 背景支持 媒介 回归 (SVR) 广泛用于流行病预测,因为核方法可以有效地模拟非线性、多变量和滞后的气候与疾病关系。虽然从业者通常应用详尽的网格搜索超参数优化,但这种计算成本高昂的调整是否在严格、无泄漏的时间序列验证下产生统计上显着的预测增强仍然是一个悬而未决的经验问题。目的 严格评估基于 SVR 的每周登革热病例预测的网格搜索超参数优化的统计意义和实用性。方法 本研究利用 1990 年至 2013 年波多黎各圣胡安和秘鲁伊基托斯公开的 DengAI 基准(N = 1,872 个城市周)构建了一条严格无泄漏的管道。该管道包含中值插补、训练专用的 Z 分数异常值缓解、标准化和主成分分析。我们将默认的 SVR 配置与针对正则化常数、ε 不敏感管和核系数进行优化的网格调整 SVR 进行了比较。应用了三种验证协议:时间顺序 80:20 保留、滚动源时间序列交叉验证以及利用五个外折叠的嵌套时间序列交叉验证。统计推断依赖于应用于外折叠误差的成对 Wilcoxon 符号秩检验,并辅以 Cohen 的 dz 效应大小、百分位引导 95% 置信区间和 Holm-Bonferroni 多重校正。通过系统地改变保留主成分的数量来检查方法的稳健性。结果 在按时间顺序保留的评估中,网格搜索将伊基托斯的平均绝对误差 (MAE) 减少了 0.30%,在圣胡安减少了 0.59%。在嵌套交叉验证下,调整模型和默认模型之间的 MAE 平均差异表明,伊基托斯的案例减少了 0.024 个案例(p = 1.0000),而圣胡安的案例增加了 0.494 个案例(p = 0.1875)。经过多重校正后,这两个结果均未达到统计显着性。此外,所选的超参数在外部验证折叠中表现出严重的不稳定,特别是对于圣胡安。优化过程还分别导致每个城市额外增加 11.48 秒和 14.80 秒的计算挂钟开销,但没有带来相应的准确性优势。结论 在 DengAI 基准测试和强大的无泄漏预处理管道的背景下,默认的 SVR 配置在统计上与其网格调整的对应配置没有区别。这些发现表明,流行病预测中的超参数优化不应自动执行。相反,它必须由预先注册的最小利益效应大小和明确的计算停止规则进行战略指导。本研究提出的综合方法框架为评估其他低倍时间序列预测领域的优化效用提供了一个潜在的可移植框架。

title: Social network analysis and exponential random graph modelling of dengue spatiotemporal linkage networks in an urban Malaysian district
abstract: Dengue burden is increasingly concentrated in rapidly urbanising Asian cities, yet routine surveillance rarely captures fine-scale residential spatiotemporal co-occurrence. We characterised a case-level linkage network and identified sociodemographic and residential correlates of linkage formation in Petaling District, Malaysia, using social network analysis and exponential random graph models (ERGMs). Cases were linked when their residences were within 200 m and symptom onset occurred within 14 days. Among 19,549 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases reported in 2023, 12,978 had at least one linkage, forming 21,424 linkages in a highly fragmented network. Linkages represent residential co-occurrence rather than confirmed transmission. Among connected cases, the conditional odds of linkage were elevated for pairs of high-rise residents (OR 6.66, 95% CI 6.40–6.93), low-rise residents (OR 4.34, 95% CI 4.15–4.54) and non-citizen cases (OR 3.96, 95% CI 3.70–4.22). Student status was modestly associated with linkage formation (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.05–1.10). Degree-related structural dependence was not supported. Attribute associations were more stable than structural dependence across evaluated network definitions. Integrating linkage analysis into routine surveillance could support targeted prioritisation of vector control in high-rise buildings and priority communities when operational capacity is constrained.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterise the spatiotemporal linkage networks of dengue cases in Petaling District, Malaysia, using social network analysis and exponential random graph models (ERGMs). The research focused on identifying sociodemographic and residential factors associated with the formation of these linkages. Among 19,549 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases in 2023, 12,978 had at least one linkage, forming 21,424 linkages in a highly fragmented network. The findings suggest that linkages reflect residential co-occurrence rather than direct transmission. The study highlights the potential of integrating linkage analysis into routine surveillance to guide targeted vector control efforts in high-rise buildings and priority communities. The results indicate that attribute associations, such as high-rise and low-rise residency, were more stable than structural dependence across evaluated network definitions. However, the evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

title: Dengue Fever Complicated by Intracerebral Haemorrhage, Acute Respiratory Failure and Nosocomial Pneumonia: A Case Report
abstract: Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne viral illness caused by the dengue virus. Majority of cases have self-limiting course, rarely severe dengue causes fatal neurological complications like encephalitis and haemorrhage. This is case report of a 38-year-old male who presented with three days of high-grade fever, one day of altered sensorium, headache, and generalised weakness. Serological testing confirmed dengue IgM positivity. The clinical course was complicated by a rapid decline in Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) from 15 to 11, necessitating endotracheal intubation on day two in the setting of blood-stained pulmonary secretions. Highresolution Computed Tomography (CT) of the thorax suggested consolidation with pulmonary oedema. CT of the brain revealed a 3.9×3.8×3.5 cm Intracerebral Parenchymal Haemorrhage (IPH) with surrounding oedema causing significant mass effect. Laboratory parameters documented severe thrombocytopaenia (nadir 0.6 lac/cumm), coagulopathy, hepatocellular injury with peak SGOT/ SGPT of 227/276 IU/L, and elevated C-reactive protein at 85.6 mg/L. Endotracheal aspirate cultures grew extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii on day five, requiring escalation of antimicrobial therapy to meropenem and polymyxin. Supportive management included platelet and Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) transfusion. The patient was successfully extubated on day nine and discharged home on day twelve. Notably, the simultaneous occurrence of dengue-associated Intracerebral Haemorrhage (ICH), acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure, and Multi-Drug Resistant (MDR) nosocomial pneumonia in a young immunocompetent adult represents a triad that is rarely documented in the published literature. Early recognition of neurological deterioration, timely neuroimaging, aggressive blood product support, and targeted antimicrobial therapy with conservative management of ICH remains critical determinants of a favourable outcome.
